messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate detected on edge-proxy (gateway) — 5xx and TLS handshake failures spiking for multiple customers. Paging #incidents. brief: 5xx rate 18% -> 40m, TLS handshake errors (SSL_connect) increasing, autoscale not helping. See metrics: https://ops.redwood.example/edge/gateway/errors

alice (oncall): ack — I'm on it. gathering context and will triage. paging bob_ops and frank_infra.

bob_ops: looking at logs now. grep of edge-proxy shows a lot of: 
```
2026-03-14T02:19:32Z edge-proxy[nginx]: 172.18.0.4:52344 SSL: error:14094412:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
2026-03-14T02:19:32Z edge-proxy[nginx]: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
```
expired cert subject CN=*.redwood-inference.internal, not the customer cert — matches mTLS client cert validation failure patterns.

frank_infra: quick check of our cert automation: acme-renewer job last succeeded 2026-03-13T23:52:01Z for edge-proxy. The vault version shows an existing cert but expiry is 2026-03-14T02:10:00Z — that would explain the spike starting ~02:12Z. ACME webhook logs show rate-limited challenge responses and a DNS provider 5xx.

alice (oncall): confirmed timeframe lines up with alert. Impact: ~30% of requests hitting edge return 503/524 depending on client timeout, customers in EU and US regions affected. Sasha, please triage support tickets and surface the highest-impact customers to SRE.

sasha_support: on it — opening ticket list and will DM affected customers being proactively notified. Tagging legal/compliance for any regulated customers.

carlos_sec: quick question — do we have any active rotation or revocation that could cause CA chain mismatch? I see a CA rotation scheduled for next week but not today. also want to know if any intermediate certs were rotated.

bob_ops: CA chain looks identical. the only anomaly is the leaf cert expiry time. `openssl s_client -connect edge-proxy.prod:443 -servername api.redwood.com` shows:
```
subject=CN = *.redwood-inference.internal
issuer=CN = Redwood Test CA
Not After : Mar 14 02:10:00 2026 GMT
```
so the proxy is serving the expired cert.

frank_infra: root cause candidate: our ACME renewer failed to complete challenge due to transient DNS provider 502s; renewer retried but didn't write the new secret. The deployment that pulls certs didn't pick up a renewed secret (it doesn't auto-reload on secret change in this cluster).

alice (oncall): mitigation options — rank them:
1) Hotpatch edge-proxy with renewed cert (from vault backup) — fast if we have a known-good cert.
2) Failover traffic to backup gateway (edge-bak) in another region — will add latency but stop errors quickly.
3) Temporarily relax mTLS validation for downstream services (risky for security) — only if other options fail.

frank_infra: I can push a hotpatch. I have a rotated cert in vault with Not After 2027-03-13. I'll fetch and apply as kubernetes secret and trigger a rolling restart of the edge-proxy daemonset. Command I will run: 
```
kubectl -n infra create secret tls edge-proxy-cert --cert=/tmp/edge.crt --key=/tmp/edge.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/edge-proxy
```
I'll do a canary on 2 pods first.

alice (oncall): do the canary, monitor errors and TLS handshakes. If canary is green, ramp to all nodes. Keep me posted every 2 minutes.

deploy-bot: deploy started by frank_infra: rollout/edge-proxy v2.1.3-canary -> 2 pods. Link: https://deploys.redwood.example/rollouts/edge-proxy/1862456792

frank_infra: canary applied. Initial telemetry: handshake error rate on canary nodes dropped from 38% -> 1.8% within 30s. requests success increased.

bob_ops: confirmed from logs on canary nodes: new cert Not After 2027-03-13. TLS handshakes succeed, no x509 expired messages.

deploy-bot: rollout progressing: 5/10 pods updated, health checks passing.

alice (oncall): start failover rollback plan standby — if anything breaks we will shift traffic to edge-bak. frank, please continue. Sasha, status on customer comms?

sasha_support: sent proactive notifications to top 12 customers affected. using standard incident template. no PII leaked.

frank_infra: rollout completed: 10/10 pods updated. Telemetry: global 5xx rate returned to baseline ~0.6% within 7 minutes of full rollout. Post-upgrade logs show clean handshakes.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: edge-proxy v2.1.3 rolled out by frank_infra at 2026-03-14T03:04:12Z.

alice (oncall): great work team. Moving to incident status: mitigated. Next: postmortem, but for now we need a short-term follow-up list: 
- frank: ensure ACME renewer has retry/backoff to avoid DNS 502 noise causing failed renews; add alert when vault cert expiry < 72h and renewer last success > 12h.
- bob: instrument secret rotation detection (auto-reload when secret changes) for edge-proxy.
- carlos: review CA/intermediate rotation schedule and ensure no overlap with renew jobs.
- sasha: finish customer notification and close tickets when customers confirm.

carlos_sec: I'll triage CA schedule and confirm no other rotations.

bob_ops: creating a runbook task to add secret watcher and a unit test that emulates renewer failure during DNS outage.

sasha_support: customers acknowledged; two flagged for post-incident SLA credits — I'll coordinate with finance.

alice (oncall): handing off to bob_ops for next 4 hours (follow-up investigation). bob, you're on-call for the post-incident until 06:15Z.

bob_ops: acknowledged, taking over. Will open a postmortem doc and link here.

incident-bot: ACTION: Incident declared mitigated at 2026-03-14T03:17:15Z. Severity: Sev2. PagerDuty incident ID: PD-8923.

alice (oncall): logging the timeline in /incidents/postmortems/PD-8923 and scheduling a 90-minute blameless postmortem for tomorrow 09:00Z. Thanks everyone. :tada:
